records.title: Louisiana Makes the Gold Debit Card Legal Tender
records.text: Landry signs Act 304: gold and silver specie and gold-backed debit instruments are Louisiana legal tender, with authority to use another state's bullion depository — Texas's, by name. It passed 84-0 and 39-0. Nobody was watching the quietest second gold state in the nation.

records.title: Missouri Is the Eighth Gold State
records.text: Kehoe signs the Constitutional Money Act: gold and silver legal tender, capital-gains exemption, anti-confiscation language. Eighth state in the belt after Utah, Wyoming, Oklahoma, Arkansas, Louisiana, Idaho, and Alabama. The wave is no longer news in the states where it happens — which is the news.

records.title: A Gold Dealer Sues Texas Over Its Own Money
records.text: Texas Precious Metals sues the Comptroller and the Bullion Depository administrator in Travis County over the Redback coin program. Not a constitutional case — a trade fight: the dealer says the state exceeded its authority, competes unlawfully with private business, and stole its trademarked Texas-outline mark. The money from below has its first casualty: the private gold market the state just walked into.

records.title: The Judge Lets Texas Keep Minting
records.text: Judge David Ezra denies the injunction against the Redback program after a three-day hearing. The merits are still alive, but the state keeps selling gold money while the case runs. A month later the Comptroller announced the 2026 series — Texas answered the lawsuit by doubling the print run.

records.title: Florida Ratifies the Gold Machine
records.text: DeSantis signs HB 1311, ratifying the CFO's rules and disarming the dead-man switch the legislature built into its own gold law — without this signature the whole thing self-repealed on June 30. Two laws, thirteen months, near-unanimous votes: the fullest custodian-depository-electronic-transfer plumbing any state has built for metal money. Live July 1.

records.title: Louisiana Opens the Bayou Gold Program
records.text: Act 841 creates a state registry of certified electronic gold-payment platforms in the Treasury. Stacked on last year's Act 304, Louisiana now has the most complete gold-money architecture outside Texas: legal tender, debit instruments, depository access, and now a certified payments network — assembled unanimously and in silence.

records.title: Texas Prints Gold Bills
records.text: The Texas Comptroller announces the 2026 Lone Star gold and silver coins and 'Modern Redbacks' — 24-karat gold bills, a state printing gold money for the first time since the Republic. It rides the new legal-tender law (HB 1056): specie becomes Texas legal tender September 1, 2026, and the comptroller's electronic gold currency may start no sooner than May 1, 2027. records.title: Gold Is Legal Tender in Florida
records.text: The gold-and-silver legal tender law takes effect — the largest state ever to do it. Gold above 99.5 percent and silver above 99.9 percent recognized as money, sales-tax exempt, with a custodian regime for electronic specie payments. Signed in May 2025, effective the week of the 250th anniversary: while Washington tokenizes the dollar from above, the big states are re-monetizing metal from below.

records.title: New Hampshire Passes the First Bitcoin Reserve Law
records.text: Ayotte signs HB 302 — the first state law in the nation letting the treasurer put public money into bitcoin, up to five percent of funds, assets over $500 billion market cap only. The treasurer's answer the next day: no plans to buy. Fourteen months later she still hasn't. First to pass, last to act — the law was the point.
